_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: Noir week, ii
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 22, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; CHLOE — aged 22, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders. WOOD wears noir dectective attire with fedora. CHLOE wears rural femme fatale. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Tuesday. Captions, not balloons. A woman in a doorway who is not Chloe and is. A cigarette he doesn't smoke. The dog is still gone. Panel 1: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a rain-slick small-town street at night with a woman in a belted coat standing in a lit doorway half in shadow and a man in a trench coat in the street, film-noir composition, heavy black (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE). caption box: "She was standing where she always stood. Which was wherever I wasn't.". Panel 2: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, close-up of a man's hand in a trench-coat sleeve holding an unlit cigarette in rain (in this panel: WOOD). caption box: "I didn't smoke. It was that kind of week.". Panel 3: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a woman turning back into a doorway as the door closes and the light narrows to a line, a man in a trench coat watching from the rain (in this panel: CHLOE). caption box: "She didn't say anything. She'd said it all in a letter I'd used as a coaster.". Panel 4: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, an empty rain-slick street at night with one man in a trench coat, the space beside him conspicuously empty, heavy black, no words (in this panel: WOOD). caption box: "The street was empty. Even the things that were usually there weren't.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR". Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @loc_main_street shows the setting; keep its architecture and props. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @loc_main_street for the setting.
